transcript.text: Please make a little mini-documentary introducing the real F-35A Lightning II, because I want it to feel like a straightforward introduction to the actual aircraft. I sometimes worry that aircraft videos end up looking more like imaginary movie jets than the real thing. What I have in mind is showing it taking off from a runway and then flying, and the whole thing should be 8 seconds long and widescreen. Put the label 'F-35A Lightning II' on it, with 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' appearing in turn. Please use calm English narration explaining those two facts, meaning that it has one engine and takes off conventionally from a runway. Keep the aircraft proportions real rather than making it look like a sci-fi jet.

Your 8-second widescreen F-35A Lightning II mini-documentary is ready:
http://127.0.0.1:8000/films/accbcf02af9f4e228855bab6735eb34f.mp4

What's in it (one continuous shot, 858x480, 16:9):
- 0–4 s: the F-35A rolls down the runway. On screen: "F-35A Lightning II" and "One engine". The narrator says: "The F-35A Lightning II is powered by a single engine."
- 4–8 s: it lifts off and climbs away. On screen: "F-35A Lightning II" and "Conventional takeoff". The narrator says: "It takes off conventionally, from a runway."
- The narration is a calm English voice, with no music.
- I asked for the real aircraft's shape: grey paint, one seat, one engine, two tails angled outward and trapezoid wings. I told it not to make a sci-fi jet.

Please check these when you watch it, because I couldn't check them myself:
- The video model drew the on-screen words itself, so a letter may be wrong (this model spelled words right 2 out of 2 times in tests). If anything is misspelled, I can remake the clip so the words come out exact, either as short title cards or on a still image that the clip starts from.
- AI video can still get the jet's shape a bit wrong. Tell me if it looks off.
- The narration runs about 8.4 seconds, so the last word may be cut a little at the end.

This used 432 credits: 192 for the video, 240 for the narration.
transcript.why: The reply presents a finished result: a link to the 8-second F-35A mini-documentary, with a description of its contents. The caveats (possible misspelled on-screen text, possible shape errors, possible cut-off narration) do not change the category, and the reply does not ask a question or wait for approval.
